source_text: So, looking at the current progress chart I see it says (only) 6 not probed yet

fragments.text: So, looking at the current progress chart I see it says (only) 6 not probed yet

reply_text:
㊥ (the 6 not-probed rows) Yes, the chart is current. zai-3's sweep has now probed almost everything: 18 of 110 compiled, 87 blocked, and 5 not probed yet (6 a moment ago). zai-3 is still on those last ones. Two causes account for most of the 87 blocked rows:
- 34 rows: stuck `Decidable (Eq ?m ?m)`.
- 29 rows: `m` unsolved before `Pure`.

㊟ (how current those 29 rows are) All 29 were probed before the fix for that error landed. 25 were probed at `6d6e824` and 4 at `62201b2`. I checked that both are older than `6af2ff5`, the commit that fixes the `m`/`Pure` stop. So those rows record a stop that is already fixed. They won't all compile now; each will show whatever stop comes next.

㊭ (next step) When zai-3's sweep finishes, I'll have those 29 rows re-probed at the current blank-startup HEAD, `91a6f5b`. That run will show what they are really blocked on now. I'll leave the 34 `Decidable` rows until the Bool-to-Prop fix is in. zai-1 is still running the discovery for it, so re-probing them now would only repeat the known stop.

previous_reply_acts.text: (what "hello world" would add) Very little on the parse side. Once the parser tables and environment exist, parsing a file with content runs the same parser code on more input. The large step after that would be elaboration. The port deliberately doesn't do elaboration yet, because it is the parse-only path.
